svg.text: A washing-machine drum with a tilt axis, exchangeable liners and a stator arm washes, peels, spins, tumbles, kneads — and cleans itself.
spin 800 rpm at r 0.15 m = 107 g
2 L detergent 55 °C, 3 min at 50 rpm, reversing

g.text: smooth, two low lifters: tumble, knead, bread balls
rasp: abrasive peeling, 1.5 kg in 2–3 min
rubber studs: slip skins after blanching
helix: mixes one way, discharges the other
small insert: 1 egg white, 100 g dough
The liner is the soiled part. The drum cleans itself like a washing
machine; the liner–shell gap is the known biofilm spot: 85 °C rinse,
spin and hot air after every use; liners to the chamber daily.
Weak point: no flat surface or orientation — no cubes, no Rouladen,
no Schnitzel, no sheets. A superb produce machine, half a kitchen.

svg.text: 1/7 Drum tilted +60°: the box tilter drops potatoes into the mouth
2/7 Tilt to 0°: water in, rasp liner tumbles the potatoes — peel flushes to the strainer
3/7 Spin 800 rpm: water is thrown off, the potatoes are dry
4/7 Tilt −30°: the potatoes roll out of the mouth into the pot
5/7 Self-clean: the stator arm becomes a spray lance — detergent wash, drain, 85 °C rinse
6/7 Spin dry, then hot air through the lance — the drum is its own dishwasher
7/7 Back to +60°, ready for the next job
